The present Detailed Accidental Report was filed qua the accident dated 22.06.2018.As per the facts of the present case, on 22.06.2018, at about 2.45 A.M,
petitioner was returning back to his house at Jai Vihar, Nazafgarh, Delhi after finished his duty.
When he reached near Jai Vihar, near Ganda Nala, Masjid Najafgarh,Delhi, a motor cycle bearing No. DL4S DG1972 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner with great force from behind.
Due to heavy impact, petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
The petitioner was removed to DDU hospital where he remained admitted wef 22.06.2018 to 18.07.20218 and was operated upon.

2. After investigation the IO found that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving of Motor cycle bearing No. DL4S DG 1972 driven by Sandeep Kumar (driver) who has been made respondent no. 1.Sh

I have heard ld. counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld Counsel for respondent No.3.

My issue wise findings are as under: ISSUE No. (i): Whether Dinesh Sahni sustained grievous injuries in the accident dt. 22.06.2018 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle bearing No. DL4S DG1972 being driven by respondent No.1 Sandeep Kumar , Owned by Respondent No.2 Vipin Bhardwaj and Insured by Respondent No.3 HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company ?
OPP 7.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.
He has examined himself as PW 1.
None of the respondents have examined any witness in support of their case.
8. PW 1 in his evidence filed by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A, has deposed that on 22.06.2018, at about 2.45 A.M, he was returning back to his house at Jai Vihar after finished his duty.

He has deposed that when he reached near Jai Vihar, near Ganda Nala, Masjid Najafgarh,Delhi, a motor cycle bearing No. DL4S DG1972 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit him with great force from behind.
He fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
He was removed to DDU hospital where he remained admitted wef 22.06.2018 to 18.07.20218.
He has deposed that in the accident he sustained fracture of IT ( Intertochanteric) of right side and injuries on other part of his body.
PW 1 has been cross examined, but nothing material could come out from his cross examination which could disbelief his testimony.
Being injured, the petitioner was the natural eyewitness of the accident.

Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing off Dinesh Kumar Sahni vs Sandeep Kumar on 10 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32024490/

It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
9. The fact that petitioner suffered injuries in that accident is also supported by his medical documents being issued by DDU Hospital, Delhi.
After investigation, police also indicted respondent no. 1 as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his alleged false implication, if any.
The fact of accident and the respondent no.1 is facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.

Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of motor cycle bearing No. DL4S DG1972 by respondent no. 1 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
ISSUE No.2: ? Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom?
Being injured, petitioner is well within his rights to claim compensation.
It is there on record, as per the deposition of PW 1 and the MLC annexed with DAR, he remain admitted in DDU hospital wef 22.06.2018 to 18.07.20218.

He has deposed that in the accident he sustained fracture of IT (
Intertochanteric) of right side and during admission he was operated upon.
After discharge he used to visit in OPD on the advise of treating Doctor.
It is deposed by him (PW1) that due to the said accident, he himself and his family members have suffered great mental pain, agony, love and affection, loss of income, loss of social activities etc.

So considering all the facts compensation is awarded as under:
MEDICAL EXPENSES 11.

The petitioner has not placed on record any medical bills but seeing the nature of injuries suffered by petitioner as well as his admission in DDU hospital and follow treatment, a lump sum amount of Rs. 10,000/ is granted to him as compensation towards medical expenses.
LOSS OF EARNING 12.It
is submitted by Ld Counsel for the Insurance company that there is no evidence qua proving monthly income of the petitioner.
In rebuttal to the submission Ld Counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner was doing private job and earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.
Petitioner has not placed on record any document qua showing his income.
No employer examined by petitioner.
So this Tribunal has assessed the income of petitioner as per Minimum Wages Act for computation of compensation.
So this Tribunal while assessing the income of injured under Minimum Wages Act prevailing in Delhi has assessed the income of injured under the head of unskilled as Rs.13,896/ p.m.
The petitioner sustained fracture of IT ( Intertochanteric) of right side.
He remained admitted in hospital wef 22.06.2018 to 18.07.20218.
After discharge he has taken follow up treatment from hospital also.

So seeing the nature of injuries on the person of petitioner,

Pain and suffering 14.

The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which he got medical treatment and he was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
Petitioner sustained fracture of IT ( Intertochanteric) of right side.
He remained admitted in hospital wef 22.06.2018 to 18.07.20218.
After discharge he he has also taken follow up treatment from other hospital also.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which he faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
To compensate petitioner under this head, a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded to him.

Mental and physical shock:
15.

The petitioner is 37 years of age at the time of accident , but due to this mishappening with him,
all his dreams and expectations got completely shattered which cannot be compensated in monetary terms.
However, to console him to an extent, a sum of Rs.30,000/ is awarded to petitioner under this head.

ISSUE No. 3 (RELIEF)
19.
Petition in hands is allowed.
Respondent no.3 is directed to pay Rs.1,89,480/with interest @
7.5% from the date of filing of DAR i.e. 27.11.2018 till the date of compliance to the petitioner as compensation in this case, within 30 days from today.
Amount of interim compensation (if any) be deducted from this amount.
The awarded amount shall remain as tax free in view of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in case in R/Special Civil Application No.4800 of 2021 titled The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd Vs Chief Commissioner of Income Tax (TDS) decided on 05.04.2022.
20.
Considering circumstances of petitioner, 10% of the amount of compensation alongwith awarded interest be released to the petitioner by way of transferring the same in his saving bank account.
The petitioner would allowed to withdraw the same through withdrawal slip only and by no other mode/modes i.e. ATM/ debit card/credit card/letter/NEFT/RTGS etc.
It is directed that 90%
of amount alongwith awarded interest of compensation be kept in the form of FDRs ie Two FDRs of equal amount in any nationalized bank ( ie petitioner's bank) in the name of petitioner for a period of one year to two years with cumulative interest.
21. The salient features as pres cribed in the judgment in Rajesh Tyagi Vs. Ramesh Chandra Gupta FAO No. 842/2009 and MAC. App. No. 422/2009 decided on 07.11.2014 are to be applied:
(i) Original fixed deposit receipt be retained by the bank in safe custody.
However, the original passbook shall be given to the claimant along with the photocopy of the FDR.
(ii) The original fixed deposit receipt be handed over to the claimant at the end of the fixed deposit period.
(iii) Photo identity card shall be issued to the claimant and the withdrawal shall be permitted only after due verification by the Bank of the identity card of the claimant.
(iv) No cheque book/ATM/debit card/credit card shall be issued to the claimant without permission of the Court.
(v) No loan, advance or withdrawal or premature encashment shall be allowed on the fixed deposit without permission of the Court.
22. Respondent no.3 is directed to deposit entire amount of compensation with this tribunal, within 30 days from today, with advance notice to petitioner.
